summary: APM feed s127_double is degraded: VLAN 20 completely missing (50% untagged) and tool port severely overloaded by 30.64 Gbps microburst on 10 Gbps port (306% capacity).

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or upstream trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags or pruning VLAN 20. 50% of packets arrive untagged and required VLAN 20 is never seen, while VLAN 10 is present, indicating tag stripping or VLAN filter misconfiguration on broker ingress/egress.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM has zero visibility into VLAN 20 application traffic and incomplete tagging for 50% of flows. Transaction tracing, segmentation by VLAN, and per-VLAN latency/error baselines will be blind/inaccurate for VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: Preserve 802.1Q tags through the packet broker and explicitly forward both required VLANs 10 and 20 to the APM so it can correctly classify and monitor all application segments.

findings.root_cause: Single 10 Gbps APM port is fed an aggregate that microbursts to 30.64 Gbps in 1ms (306% of capacity, >80% threshold). Broker is sending full feed to one tool port with no load balancing or burst buffering, exceeding line rate.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will drop packets randomly during bursts due to port overrun/buffer exhaustion. Results in incomplete flows, missed transactions, inaccurate latency and error rates, and degraded detection of performance anomalies.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple APM tool ports/instances via hash-based load balancing to keep each port under ~70-80% of 10 Gbps even during 30+ Gbps bursts, preventing drops while preserving both directions per flow for APM.
